title: tessera configuration
description: The configuration file of tessera, an external authorization service for Envoy. This schema checks key names, types, allowed values, integer bounds and the form of some strings. It does not check the rules that involve two keys (such as two listeners on the same port), the syntax of hosts and socket paths, or environment variables: a string value can take text from the environment with ${NAME} or ${NAME:-default}, and such a value is checked only after substitution. `tessera config validate` is the authority on whether a file is valid.

listen.description: The address of the gRPC listener: host:port, or unix: followed by the path of a socket, relative to the configuration file when it is not absolute.

max_connections.description: The largest number of open connections from Envoy to the gRPC listener; a connection beyond it is closed at once.

max_concurrent_streams.description: The largest number of concurrent calls on one connection from Envoy.

max_connection_age.description: The age at which a connection from Envoy is closed gracefully, so that the load spreads across replicas. 0s sets no limit.

drain_delay.description: At shutdown, the time between reporting not ready and closing the connections.

shutdown_timeout.description: At shutdown, the longest time to finish the calls in progress. Positive.

admin.description: The listener of the health checks and the metrics.

listen.description: The address of the admin listener, as host:port. It must not share its address and port with server.listen.

log.description: The log events, written to standard output.

level.description: The lowest level of the events that are written.

format.description: The format of the events: one line of key=value pairs, or one JSON object per line.

decisions.description: The decisions that a decision event reports: none; deny, the denials, and the allows in which an audit rule with action deny matched; or all.

client_ip.description: Where tessera reads the client address of a request: from one source, without falling back on another.

from.description: The source of the client address: peer, the address of the connection to Envoy; header, a header that holds one address; x_forwarded_for, the X-Forwarded-For header, read from the right.

header.description: The header that holds the client address, in any case. Required, and allowed only, when from is header.

trusted_hops.description: The number of entries at the right end of X-Forwarded-For that trusted proxies wrote after the client address. Required, and allowed only, when from is x_forwarded_for.

sets.description: The named sets that conditions read with sets.<name>.contains(value). A name is a lowercase letter followed by lowercase letters, digits and underscores, at most 63 characters, and not a reserved word of the expression language.

type.description: The type of the values: cidr, IP networks and addresses; asn, autonomous system numbers; string, strings compared exactly.

values.description: The values of the set, written here: strings, or for an asn set integers too. A set has one source: values or file.

file.description: The file of the set, relative to the configuration file when it is not absolute: one value per line, # starts a comment. A set has one source: values or file.

refresh.description: How often tessera checks the file for a change. At least 1s. Only with file.

max_staleness.description: The age of the last successful check of the file beyond which the set is unavailable. 0s sets no limit; any other value must be longer than refresh. Only with file.

on_unavailable.description: What contains answers when the set is unavailable: fail makes the condition indeterminate, which counts against allowing; match answers true; no_match answers false. Only with file.

max_entries.description: The largest number of values of the set, duplicates included; more is an error.

mode.description: enforce applies the decisions; audit allows every request, and reports the denials it did not enforce with enforced=false, in the decision event and in tessera_decisions_total.

default_action.description: The decision for a request that no rule decides. It has no default, so that every configuration states whether such requests are allowed or denied.

deny_response.description: What Envoy answers the client when a request is denied, unless the rule that denies it states otherwise.

status.description: The HTTP status of a denial.

body.description: The body of a denial, at most 8 KiB. Envoy adds content-type: text/plain to a body when the headers have no content-type.

headers.description: The headers of a denial, by name. A header that Envoy sets itself or that describes the connection, such as content-length, is not allowed.

rules.description: The rules, evaluated in order: the first whose condition is true decides. At most 1000.

name.description: The name of the rule: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, at most 63 characters, unique. default is reserved.

description.description: A description of the rule, at most 1024 bytes.

action.description: What the rule does with the requests it matches.

mode.description: enforce lets the rule decide; audit never lets it decide: a true condition shows in audit_rules of the decision event and in tessera_audit_matches_total, and tessera goes on to the next rule.

when.description: The condition of the rule, a CEL expression whose result is a bool. Without it, the rule matches every request.

response.description: The response of a deny rule: each key it does not write comes from policy.deny_response. Not allowed on an allow rule.

status.description: The HTTP status of the denial. By default, policy.deny_response.status.

body.description: The body of the denial, at most 8 KiB. By default, policy.deny_response.body.

headers.description: The headers of the denial, which replace policy.deny_response.headers as a whole. By default, policy.deny_response.headers.

duration.description: A duration with units, such as 500ms, 30s, 5m or 1h30m. Write 0s for zero: a number without a unit is an error.

environment.description: A string that takes all or part of its value from the environment, with ${NAME} or ${NAME:-default}. The value is checked after substitution.
